correctness.rationale: A common reset couples any two initial states, giving uniqueness of the exponential-age stationary law. Bounded stationary displacement and angular reflection justify the stationary moment identities and centering. An independent symbolic real sine/cosine hierarchy reproduced the two moments, entire denominator H and all six coefficients of Q. For each positive delta, H is positive and Q increases strictly from a negative constant to infinity. Variance is strictly positive. The scaled limits Q_delta(c delta)/delta -> 24c-192 and Q_delta(c/delta)/delta^3 -> 576c-4032 trap the unique root between any fixed constants on either side of 8 and 7 in the respective scaled variables. For fixed delta the dimensionless moments are asymptotic to 4 delta rho^(-3) and 960 delta^2 rho^(-6), so the ratio tends to 60 and the excess to 57 even as both moments vanish. This agrees with the independent short-age picture: the angular linearization gives a time-integrated Brownian motion of variance (2 delta/3)t^3 and conditional Gaussian fourth moment, then exponential-age mixing gives the factors 3! and 6!. Physical cumulants scale by (v/kappa)^4. Replay: python /workspace/independent_checks.py 1 (SymPy); original checker.py and VERIFICATION.md inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: A fixed reset heading makes the transverse marginal a natural anisotropic diagnostic that radial data can hide. The all-diffusivity root theorem rules out multiple transverse reversals rather than merely reproducing sampled signs. The two scaling laws locate the reset threshold in opposite physical regimes and the rapid-reset limit distinguishes shrinking fluctuations from standardized shape. A sign of excess alone is not a claim about distribution tails.
